{{short description|Finnish mathematician}}
'''Pekka Pertti Tukia''' (born 3 November 1945 in [[Pihtipudas]]<ref>{{Cite book | editor=Ellonen, Leena | title=Suomen professorit 1640–2007 Finlands professorer | page=753 | location=Helsinki | publisher=Professoriliitto | year=2008 | isbn=978-952-99281-1-8 | language=Finnish, Swedish }}</ref>) is a Finnish mathematician<ref>{{cite web|title=Tukia, Pekka|website=University of Helsinki |url=https://wiki.helsinki.fi/display/mathstatHenkilokunta/Tukia%2C+Pekka}}</ref> who does research on [[Kleinian group]]s and their geometric properties (such as [[limit set]]s).

Tukia received his PhD in 1972 with thesis advisor Kaarlo Virtanen in Helsinki.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id = 58642}}</ref> Tukia is a professor at the [[University of Helsinki]].

He made substantial contributions to the collective work of about a dozen mathematicians who proved the Seifert fiber space conjecture.<ref>{{cite arXiv|author=Préaux, Jean-Philippe|title=A survey on Seifert fibre space conjecture|eprint=1202.4142|year=2012|class=math.AT}}</ref> In 1992 he was an invited speaker with talk ''Generalizations of Fuchsian and Kleinian groups'' at the European Congress of European Mathematicians in Paris. In 1994 he was an invited speaker with talk ''A survey of Möbius groups'' at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Zürich]].
